articles.title: GHSA: OpenTelemetry Java Instrumentation: JDBC Auto-Instrumentation Logging Clear-Text Passwords
articles.summary: OpenTelemetry Java Instrumentation JDBC auto-instrumentation may fail to sanitize passwords in SQL CONNECT statements when the password is double-quoted. As a result, clear-text database passwords can be added to trace span attributes and exported to observability backends.

articles.title: GHSA: OpenTelemetry Javaagent RMI context propagation allows resource exhaustion
articles.summary:
The RMI context propagation payload reader limits the number of context entries but does not limit the aggregate size of the strings read from the stream.

An attacker who can reach an RMI endpoint on an instrumented JVM can send an oversized context propagation payload. This can cause excessive memory allocation while the JVM reads the payload, potentially leading to denial of service.

articles.title: GHSA: Easy!Appointments appointments/store and appointments/update allow cross-provider appointment injection — Authorization Bypass
articles.summary:
## Summary
 
Easy!Appointments correctly filters provider-scoped appointments in the `appointments/search` response, proving that provider isolation is an intended security boundary. However, the direct mutation endpoints `appointments/store` and `appointments/update` only check generic appointment privileges and never verify that the submitted `id_users_provider` belongs to the current session.

articles.title: GHSA: swagger-typescript-api vulnerable to authorization-token exfiltration via spec `$ref`
articles.summary:
### Summary

When the developer supplies an `--authorizationToken` (commonly required to fetch a private spec behind authentication), `swagger-typescript-api` attaches that token to the `Authorization` header of **every** subsequent HTTP request it makes while resolving external `$ref` URLs in the spec — with **no same-origin check, no host allowlist, and no scope-down** for cross-origin requests.
